newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong stocks surge in morning trade.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong stocks surge in morning trade.

text.p: Hong Kong share prices surged in morning trade on Friday, with Hang Seng Bank Ltd leading the way as it advanced into record territory on talk that a mainland company could buy a stake in the company.
The blue chip Hang Seng Index was up 365.19 points, or 2.52 percent, at 14,871.68 after rising to an early high of 14,892.32 points.
"It's all across the board but Hang Seng Bank is just incredible," said Kent Rossiter, institutional sales manager at Nikko Securities.
Shares in Hang Seng Bank surged HK$8.25 to a record high of HK$105.00, crossing HK$100 for the first time.
"It's riding on rumours that a mainland company will take a stake," said Rossiter.
Property stocks also made hefty gains with Sun Hung Kai Properties up HK$1.75 at HK$91.75 and Cheung Kong (Holdings) advancing HK$1.50 to HK$76.00.
Rossiter said the Hang Seng Index could reach a new record before Hong Kong returns to Chinese rule on July 1.
The blue chip index hit a record intra-day high of 15,020.96 points earlier this month.
FPB Bank was among the most actively traded stocks and gained HK$0.30 to HK$5.55 while International Bank of Asia rose HK$0.50 to HK$7.90.
"Every bank is having a go as a potential red chip bank," said Geoff Galbraith, institutional sales trader at Nava SC Securities.
The Hang Seng China-Affiliated Corporations Index was up 58 points, or 1.90 percent, at 3,114.
China Everbright-IHD rose HK$0.40 to HK$17.90 and China Resources gained HK$1.00 to HK$31.10.

Shares in Furama Hotel Enterprises soared HK$6.20 to HK$32.20. Lai Sun Development said it had agreed to buy a 45.42 percent stake in the company for HK$3.13 billion and would make a general cash offer for the remaining shares at HK$33.50 each.
Lai Sun Development rose HK$0.60 to HK$9.10 and subsidiary Lai Sun Hotels gained HK$0.10 to HK$2.30.
Market turnover was about HK$7.15 billion after the first hour of trade.
